issue: After the LOW-tier fix in commit eebbc25 (max_position_pct units bug: was position_limit_pct*100=2000% no-op clamp, now the fraction 0.20=20%), the PositionSizer.max_position_pct clamp is suddenly ACTIVE for all engine-driven trades. This is a 10-100x reduction in max order notional. Did this silently regress live/paper trade sizing, and is the new 20% clamp actually correct given the rest of the sizing pipeline (kelly_fraction, signal strength, fee deduction, min_order_notional)?

root_cause.hypothesis: H1 (confirmed): The eebbc25 max_position_pct units fix (position_limit_pct*100 -> position_limit_pct) activates a previously-no-op 20% clamp for engine-driven trades. This is the INTENDED enforcement of the risk config, not a regression. The pre-fix *100 (2000% cap) was the actual latent defect present since v1.0 (44b98c9), silently ignoring position_limit_pct. Default-path trades (engine win_rate=0.5 -> 12.5% sizing) are unaffected; only high-win-rate strategies (win_rate>~0.62) get correctly capped at 20% instead of exceeding it (e.g. win_rate=0.7: 27.45% -> 20%). Per-symbol signal consolidation (engine.py:189-200) makes the clamp a correct per-symbol limit matching position_limit_pct's documented semantics.
